subject: Acme trial: procurement & billing path
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Acme trial: procurement & billing path

Hi Oliver —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery so you have everything in one place: 

Recap of success criteria (from the call):
- Validate integration with two pilot teams (Search and Customer Support)
- 95th percentile latency under 500ms for typical prompts
- Cost per interaction within target range (we discussed ~ $0.03–$0.06/query)
- Achieve 3 production-ready flows within the 30-day trial window

Procurement / billing options we discussed:
- PO / invoice (preferred by your procurement) — typical turnaround 2–3 weeks depending on approvals
- Card up front — fastest to get you started immediately, can be transitioned to PO later
- Marketplace purchase (if you prefer cloud marketplace) — tends to add procurement approvals and delays

Immediate next steps I can take:
1) Send a one-page commercial summary + quote you can share with procurement (I attached the trial scope + quote stub).
2) If you want to go PO route, send your PO template so our finance team can pre-fill vendor info and return a completed quote.
3) Loop Laura (CS) into onboarding to scope pilot integrations.

Attachments: trial_scope_v1.pdf (trial scope, sample SOW + quote ranges)

If you can confirm which billing route you prefer (PO vs card vs marketplace) and the internal approver for procurement, I’ll get the right docs over today.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot started.
—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks, Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from procurement and engineering: 

- Procurement: We prefer to do a PO / Net30 invoice for vendor onboarding. I attached our standard PO template for your finance team to review. Is Redwood able to accept Net30? We also need Redwood's W-9 and SOC2 or equivalent security attestations.
- Engineering: For the trial billing start date, can we delay billing until we move into the pilot phase (we expect that around 9/15)? We want to avoid paying during the initial evaluation period.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme trial: procurement & billing path

Thanks, Oliver — looping in Laura (Customer Success) and Vivek (Sales Ops) to confirm timelines and vendor docs.

Procurement options and timeline (our experience):
- Card: immediate onboarding once payment is provided — best if you want to start the trial this week.
- PO/Net30: our finance team requires a completed PO template and W-9; once submitted we typically return a signed quote within 2–5 business days, and the PO process can take 7–21 calendar days depending on internal approvals.
- Marketplace: longer timelines due to reseller/marketplace paperwork and SSO mapping.

Billing start date: we can agree to a billing start of 2026-09-15 for the pilot period, provided a PO is received and agreed terms are in place by then. If you prefer to start earlier and use a corporate card temporarily, we can convert billing to an invoice/PO mid-trial.

Trial-to-paid conversion criteria (proposal):
- Minimum pilot usage: average >= 5k generated tokens/day OR 3 production-ready flows
- Performance: 95th percentile latency < 500ms for key routes
- Business: stakeholder sign-off by product and platform (email confirmation is fine)

Related links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345/ACME-2026-111

Next steps I will do today:
- Send a one-page commercial quote and pre-fill your PO template for faster signature (I’ll ask finance to complete and return).
- Send W-9 and SOC2 link for your vendor file.
- Laura will reach out to schedule onboarding alignment next week.
—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

We can proceed with the PO route. A few items we need to complete vendor onboarding: 
1) Completed W-9 for Redwood Inference
2) SOC2 Type II report or a letter confirming controls (can be a hosted link)

If Redwood prefers to start immediately on card, we can do that to begin the pilot and follow up with a PO for the remainder. Marketplace purchases will take longer due to additional reseller paperwork.
